quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Which of the following distracts drivers and increases crash risk?
questions.explanation: Cell phones and audio devices like radios and CD players can distract you while driving. This distraction increases your risk of crashing.

questions.question: When driving on highways, you should:

options.text: Be ready to react to road hazards.

questions.explanation: On highways, stay alert and keep your eyes moving to avoid highway hypnosis. Do not look at one thing for more than a few seconds. Be ready to react to unexpected hazards.

questions.question: You feel angry after a problem at work. Before driving home, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive.
Stop at a bar and have drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, calm down before you drive. Driving while emotional is dangerous to you and others on the road.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you. You should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.
Stop your vehicle and block the emergency vehicle.
Give the emergency vehicle a clear path to travel.
Signal the emergency vehicle when it is safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the emergency vehicle a clear path to travel.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, clear the way. Pull to the side of the road if it is safe to do so and let the vehicle pass.

questions.question: U-turns are not allowed:

options.text: In a curve in the road.
On a hill where you cannot see 500 feet ahead in both directions.
Near a sign that says no U-turns.

questions.explanation: U-turns are not allowed in curves, on hills with less than 500 feet of visibility in each direction, or near signs that prohibit U-turns.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what keeps you safe to drive?

options.text: Get a ride home from a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home from a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to get a ride from someone who has not been drinking. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol in your body. It takes about one hour for your body to eliminate one drink.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes or exiting. Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder. Make sure the lane is clear before you move.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes is:

options.text: Not needed if you use your mirror.

questions.explanation: Checking your blind spot by looking over your shoulder is a good habit. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: Make sure your passengers have fastened their seat belts:

options.text: Only when it rains or snows.
When a police officer stops you.

questions.explanation: Seat belts protect you in a crash. Make sure you and all passengers have fastened your seat belts before starting the engine.

questions.question: Stopping distance on slippery roads is:

options.text: About the same as on dry pavement.
Two to 10 times longer than on dry pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two to 10 times longer than on dry pavement.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, stopping takes two to 10 times longer than on dry pavement. Drive slowly and carefully on wet or icy surfaces.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a roundabout is ahead. Slow down and enter the roundabout at a low speed. Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.question: When you are in a travel lane on the roadway:

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you miss the freeway entrance ramp.
Don't stop for any reason. Keep driving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't stop for any reason. Keep driving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep driving until you can safely leave the road. If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Continue to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no warning signals (like flashing lights or gates), a driver should slow down, look, and listen.
questions.explanation: At railroad crossings with no warning devices or only a crossbuck sign, slow down. Look both directions on the track and listen for trains or railroad equipment. Only cross when it is safe.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles must use the full lane width like all other vehicles.

questions.question: Night driving is more difficult than daytime driving because:

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
You cannot see as far in the dark.
It rains more often at night.
You are more likely to see motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you can see less distance ahead. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough so you can stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: This sign tells you that:

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road has three or more curves ahead.

questions.question: "Highway hypnosis" is a driving condition caused by:

options.text: Staring straight ahead at the road for a long time.
Getting too much sleep the night before.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring straight ahead at the road for a long time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead without checking side mirrors and blind spots. You zone out and may hit traffic that slows or stops in front of you.

questions.question: When you see this black and yellow sign, it means:

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right due to roadwork.
Slow down because the road ahead makes a sharp turn at an extreme angle.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road ahead makes a sharp turn at an extreme angle.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road turns sharply ahead. Slow down as you would for a sharp turn at an intersection.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train. You must stop if:
questions.explanation: Stop before crossing railroad tracks if red lights flash, a gate is down, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is visible or very close. If you are not sure it is safe, stop. Never try to beat a train.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street the wrong way.
Do not drive in this lane.
Left-turning traffic on a green light must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left-turning traffic on a green light must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign with a traffic signal means left-turning traffic does not have the right-of-way. You must wait for oncoming traffic to clear before turning left.

questions.question: When sharing the road with large commercial vehicles, you should:

options.text: Know that large vehicles need extra time and space to slow down and stop.
Remember that commercial vehicles have large blind spots.
Signal your turns and lane changes well in advance.

questions.explanation: Large trucks and buses use air brakes. Air brakes work slower than regular brakes, so these vehicles need more time and space to stop. Large vehicles also have bigger blind spots than smaller cars. Always signal before turning or changing lanes.

questions.question: A steady green light at an intersection means that you:

options.text: Must slow down and get ready to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before going.
Can drive through the intersection if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can drive through the intersection if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through the intersection if the road is clear. You can also turn right or left on a steady green light unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians go first.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Is snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Stops the seat belt alarm from sounding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should be snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: Not getting enough sleep affects your driving ability the same way as:
questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol affect your driving the same way. Being awake for 18 hours impairs driving about as much as having a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours straight affects driving like having a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: Don't follow other cars too closely because:

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front of you slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the turn signals.
You may not see the brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front of you slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the car in front stops suddenly, you may not have enough time to stop and could crash into it.

questions.question: A sign of a drunk driver is:
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving slower than traffic, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking the rearview mirror.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.explanation: Signal your left turn three to five seconds before the intersection. Keep checking your rearview mirror as you slow down. On roads with multiple lanes, move to the left lane before you reach the intersection. Wait for traffic and pedestrians to clear, then turn when it is safe.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm out, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn before passing on the left side.
Keep driving when you think the children are done exiting.
Pass the bus before the door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: When a school bus shows its stop signal, you must come to a complete stop. Do not move until the stop arm is pulled back in.

questions.question: Drivers are not required to yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk.
questions.explanation: You must stop and yield to pedestrians in a marked crosswalk. You must also yield to pedestrians in unmarked crosswalks on your side of the road when there are no traffic signals.

questions.question: When a curb is painted ____, it means a handicap parking spot is reserved.
questions.explanation: Painted curbs show parking rules. A blue curb marks a handicap parking spot. Only people with the correct license plate or permit can park there.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you while driving?

options.text: It makes you feel overly confident.
It reduces your ability to think clearly.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It makes you feel overly confident and careless. Alcohol also slows your reaction time, reduces coordination, and harms your balance. Your vision and ability to judge distance get worse, making it hard to react to what is around you.

questions.question: At a stop sign without a crosswalk, drivers must stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, you must make a complete stop at the stop line if there is one. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:
questions.explanation: Octagonal signs are always stop signs. Come to a complete stop when you see a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, you should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Leave more space between your car and the car ahead.

questions.explanation: In snow, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Leave extra space between your car and others because wet, cold roads make it harder for your car to stop.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing, you should:
questions.explanation: When you see signs for a railroad crossing, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not try to drive around the gate.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Sit in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down on the highway, turn on your hazard flashers. Carefully drive off the road and park where other drivers can see you easily. Raise your hood so drivers know your car is disabled.

questions.question: You cannot pass a school bus when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: When you see a school bus with flashing red lights, you must stop before reaching it and stay stopped until the lights turn off. On roads with a median or center lane, vehicles on the opposite side do not have to stop.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread depth.
Make sure your tires are filled to the right pressure.
Slow down when driving in the rain.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires in good condition with proper tread and correct air pressure. Slow down when driving in rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at higher speeds.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road turns sharply right, then left.
The road turns sharply left, then right.
The road curves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road ahead will turn sharply to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: You may not park:

options.text: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
More than 12 inches from the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must park within 12 inches of the edge of the road.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can hurt your driving. You may not drive well if you are worried, excited, afraid, angry, or sad. Stress makes it hard to concentrate on driving. Wait to drive until you feel calm and in control.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs indicate?

options.text: The fastest or slowest speed you are legally allowed to drive.
The speed you should drive in heavy traffic.
The speed you should drive in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest speed you are legally allowed to drive.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the fastest and slowest safe speeds allowed on a road. The maximum speed is for perfect conditions. You must slow down when conditions are not safe.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Change lanes as few times as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells you not to enter the road or driveway from your direction. It is not safe. If you see this sign, turn around and find another way.

questions.question: Seat belts work best when worn by:

options.text: Everyone in the car, every time you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the car, every time you drive.
questions.explanation: Everyone in your car should wear a seat belt every time. In a crash, a person without a seat belt becomes a projectile and can hurt others in the car.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. This helps other drivers know what you are doing and prevents accidents.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can make both stronger. It is dangerous to drive after using alcohol or drugs. It is even more dangerous when you use both together.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Are better drivers because they are not hungry.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These activities take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers who do these things have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their cars.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your car in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn into an exit. If you miss your exit, continue to the next one.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that you are approaching a T intersection where you may need to turn left or right.
